top_story.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement commits $278 million to deportation charter flights with CSI Aviation
top_story.dek: A single call order dated October 31 is the largest new contract action in today's data.
paragraphs: Immigration and Customs Enforcement obligated $277,971,276 to CSI Aviation, Inc. on October 31, 2026, according to USAspending. The order's description says it 'obtains dedicated and on-demand chartered flight services for enforcement and removal operations under the ICE Air Program.' The same description says the program 'facilitates the safe, secure, and cost-effective transportation and deportation of illegal aliens.' The dollar figure is the amount obligated so far.

USAspending classifies the work as air passenger transportation and the company's business as travel arrangement and reservation services. The record does not say whether the order was competed. CSI Aviation also appears in this edition's Lobbying × Contracts section as a registered federal lobbying client.

sections.headline: Commerce Department adds $35.4 million to Accenture Federal Services' 20-year financial-system contract without competition
paragraphs: Five new sole-source justifications came in today, two of them posted as Special Notices. None repeats an earlier edition. One is a contract extension and is covered in Extensions, so four are written up here.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Commerce Department raises Accenture Federal Services' financial-system contract by $35.4 million, saying only the incumbent can do the work
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of Commerce wants to raise the value of its Business Applications Solution contract with Accenture Federal Services LLC. The contract was awarded on April 24, 2020 at $340,914,621.69 after full and open competition, with a base year and 19 option years, and is now in option year six. The justification says the modification covers extra post-launch support for the National Institute of Standards and Technology, added Sunflower, PRISM and Oracle E-Business Suite licenses, and related maintenance and hosting. It says user populations grew by an average of more than 80 percent across the programs. It argues that 'Since this contractor has specifically configured the system, no other contractor has the required knowledge of, or access to, their system.'
Also worth a look

items: Transportation Department raises Veritium Ingenuity's IT support contract ceiling by $7 million to $57 million without competition. The justification cites return-to-office staffing increases and moving the Federal Aviation Administration into department headquarters, and says no funds are obligated on the contract itself. (693JK420D500001_P00007)

Defense Information Systems Agency plans to sole-source $3.7 million of 3.45 GHz spectrum coordination engineering to incumbent Peraton. Posted as a Special Notice of intent, it says Peraton has supported the mission since 2022 and is 'the only known source capable' of the work. Only the notice text was available, not the attached justification. (632775910)

items: International Trade Commission renews a $130,000 enterprise Financial Times online license without competition, posted as a Special Notice (ITC-2600-OARS-27-08)

sections.headline: Bureau of Prisons keeps Naphcare running at its Brooklyn detention center for November while a contract protest is pending
paragraphs: One new extension today: a one-month bridge for medical services at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.

blocks.title: Bureau of Prisons extends Naphcare's Brooklyn jail medical contract without competition while a protest holds up the replacement
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Prisons
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Prisons wants incumbent Naphcare to keep providing inpatient and outpatient facility and physician services to inmates at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn from November 1 to November 30, 2026. The estimated cost is $889,017.86, through monthly purchase orders at its prior Medicare benchmark rates. The justification says 'Award of a CMS contract is pending the resolution of a protest,' and that a requirements contract is anticipated. The performance period began the day before the notice was posted. The pipeline's log shows an earlier Naphcare interim-services justification at the same $889,018 value.

sections.headline: General Services Administration posts a $27 million furniture-schedule award to The Bread and Butter Brand Consulting LLC
paragraphs: Nine new award notices, three flagged and six routine. None was already reported.

blocks.title: General Services Administration awards a $27 million Multiple Award Schedule contract to a company named Brand Consulting
meta: The Bread and Butter Brand Consulting LLC
blocks.text: The General Services Administration's Federal Acquisition Service furniture systems division posted a $27,000,000 award on November 2, 2026 under its Multiple Award Schedule, award number 47QRAA27D0016. The awardee is The Bread and Butter Brand Consulting LLC. Its name reads like a consulting firm rather than a furniture maker. The schedule's solicitation was listed in an earlier edition on October 13, and this notice names the winner. The amount is as posted by the agency.

items: Navy's Military Sealift Command gives Detyens Shipyards $23.2 million for fiscal 2027 overhaul work on fleet oiler USNS Leroy Grumman. The award is dated October 30. (N3220527C0012)
Navy's Military Sealift Command gives Detyens Shipyards $11.8 million for fiscal 2027 work on USNS Robert F. Kennedy. The award is dated October 30. (N3220527C1259)

sections.headline: Navy seeks a shipyard for fleet oiler USNS Earl Warren's 2027 overhaul in Seventh Fleet waters, excluding India

The flagged Vienna embassy signage notice matched a keyword on the word 'emergency' and is routine.

blocks.title: Navy opens bidding for USNS Earl Warren repair and maintenance work in May to July 2027, barring work in India
meta: Offers due December 2, 2026, 1:00 PM Singapore time
blocks.text: Naval Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center Yokosuka, Singapore site, has a new requirement for repair and maintenance work on the fleet oiler USNS Earl Warren (T-AO 207). The work runs May to July 2027 in the U.S. Seventh Fleet area, with a 'geographical restriction excluding performance in India.' Interested contractors must request the package, which is sent through DoDSAFE. One attached file is queued for reading in a later edition.

items: Federal Highway Administration seeks small-business bids for bridge and pavement preservation across Northeast national park sites. The sites include the Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt, Eleanor Roosevelt and Vanderbilt Mansion national historic sites and Fire Island National Seashore, across counties in New York, New Hampshire and Massachusetts. (693C73-27-B-000003)

blocks.text: Flagged and not written up: the Mombasa voyage repair amendment (repeat) and the Vienna embassy signage notice (routine). 47 routine solicitations: Navy supply and ship-repair offices 29, Defense Logistics Agency 7, State Department embassies 5, Veterans Affairs 3, Federal Aviation Administration 1, NASA 1, Bureau of Reclamation 1. 1 repeat from earlier editions left out.

sections.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement seeks box meals for up to 72 detainees a day at its Atlanta intake unit
paragraphs: 71 new combined synopsis/solicitations, 1 flagged, and 150 repeats from earlier editions left out. The lead item comes from a statement of work read today on a notice posted earlier.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement wants three box meals a day for up to 72 detainees at its Atlanta Field Office intake unit
meta: Department of Homeland Security, Detention Compliance and Removals
blocks.text: Immigration and Customs Enforcement's Detention Compliance and Removals office is buying packaged food. The statement of work says the purpose is 'to provide box lunches three times per day 7 days a week (breakfast, lunch and dinner) for up to 72 detainees daily to the Atlanta Field Office, Detention Intake Processing Unit.' Offers must use General Services Administration Federal Supply Schedule meals. The file was posted October 21 and read in today's run.

items: Pentagon's Washington Headquarters Services asks industry about modeling and simulation support for the Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation office. The office advises the Secretary of War on program costs and force structure. (HQ003427AOI5)

Forest Service buys 1,008 Broadcom VMware Cloud Foundation licenses for its FireCloud migration to Microsoft Azure. The attached justification says vendor-specific licenses are required. This is from a file read today on a notice posted earlier. (12760426Q0213)

blocks.text: 70 routine combined synopsis/solicitations: Defense Logistics Agency Land and Maritime 46, Defense Logistics Agency Aviation 10, NASA 2, and 12 others from Navy, Air Force, Army, Bureau of Prisons, Forest Service, Federal Prison Industries and Veterans Affairs offices, one each. 150 repeats from earlier editions left out.

sections.headline: NASA's draft request for proposals would pool vendors to design non-terrestrial nuclear reactors
paragraphs: 11 new presolicitations. Both flagged ones were already listed in earlier editions and are left out: the Marine Corps notice of intent to sole-source parachute training support to Skydive Elsinore, and the Air Force area of interest for the F-47 campus at Nellis Air Force Base. The items below come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: NASA drafts a contract pool for non-terrestrial nuclear reactor design under its Space Power and Reactor Capabilities program
meta: National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Glenn Research Center
blocks.text: NASA's Glenn Research Center is running a competitive procurement to 'establish a pool of MAIDIQ vendors' that will then compete for task orders. According to the attached document, the contract's scope 'generally provides for wide-ranging support with regard the design and development of non-terrestrial nuclear reactor systems.' The file was posted August 30.

blocks.title: Navy plans a design-bid-build power plant at Chabelley Airfield in Djibouti
blocks.text: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Atlantic intends to issue a request for proposals for a firm-fixed-price, design-bid-build contract to construct a power plant and electrical distribution system at Chabelley Airfield, Djibouti. The presolicitation says solicitation documents will not be available until approximately November 5, 2026.

blocks.title: State Department's Sapporo consulate plans a 'Freedom 250' reception with fireworks at the Snow Festival
meta: Department of State, American Consulate Sapporo
blocks.text: The U.S. Consulate General in Sapporo plans a firm-fixed-price contract for 'comprehensive event management, venue, hospitality, entertainment, fireworks, permitting, transportation, parking' for the Freedom 250 event. The notice says the solicitation is not yet ready to be issued. The file name refers to the 2027 Sapporo snow sculpture.

items: Veterans Affairs plans a $20 million to $50 million set-aside for veteran-owned small businesses to upgrade health-record infrastructure at Perry Point, Maryland. The solicitation is due in mid-November 2026, with about 689 days of work. (36C77626R0118)

blocks.text: 9 routine presolicitations: Defense Logistics Agency Aviation 2, plus one each from National Institutes of Health, Defense Logistics Agency Land and Maritime, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and four Army and Navy offices. 2 flagged repeats left out.

sections.headline: Army asks industry for a ready-made tracked 155mm howitzer as a prototype award
paragraphs: 8 new special notices, 3 flagged. The Air Force white-paper request for secure trailers at Arnold Engineering Development Complex was already listed on November 1 and is left out.

blocks.title: Army seeks a mature tracked self-propelled 155mm howitzer from existing production lines
blocks.text: Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal is seeking a 'mature and available' Mobile Tactical Cannon-Tracked system with testing, safety and evaluation already completed. It plans one or more Other Transaction prototype awards under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and reserves the right to award to all, part or none of the bidders. The notice carries 30 files: 20 are queued for a later edition and 10 are access-restricted on SAM.gov.

blocks.title: Department of War asks industry for ideas on hardening and surviving attacks on military infrastructure
blocks.text: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Energy, Installations, and Environment issued a request for information on 'Resilient Infrastructure and Layered Passive Survivability.' The attached document lists four focus areas. The first, Advanced Materials and Physical Hardening, aims to protect assets and personnel from kinetic impacts. This is from a file read today on a notice posted earlier.

blocks.title: Navy aviation holds a two-day industry day on autonomy and 'super intelligence'
blocks.text: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division invites government, industry and academic leaders to an industry day on December 8 and 9, 2026 at the UMD SMART Conference Center in California, Maryland. The event focuses on autonomy and super intelligence and artificial intelligence for naval aviation. Attendance is capped at three people per organization.

items: Coast Guard plans to renew Keysight Technologies' maintenance on a satellite-navigation jamming and spoofing simulator without competition. The notice says the simulator tests Coast Guard GPS receivers, and responses are due November 5. This is from a file read today on a notice posted earlier. (52800PR270000109)

blocks.text: 5 routine special notices: Army Corps of Engineers districts at Louisville and New Orleans, 1 each; Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command, 1; Department of Defense, 1; Veterans Affairs, 1. 1 flagged repeat left out.

sections.headline: Navy signals it will buy Triton drone hydraulic servicing equipment from its original maker or authorized dealers
paragraphs: 9 new sources-sought notices, including the General Services Administration notice moved here from the D.C. tag. Four were flagged, but three (the Navy 7th Fleet welding program and two Transportation Command Pacific airlift notices for Wake Island and Kwajalein) were already listed in earlier editions and are left out. The Coast Guard and other late items come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Navy intends to limit MQ-4C Triton hydraulic servicing equipment purchase to Hydraulic International and its authorized dealers
blocks.text: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division at Lakehurst, New Jersey says it intends a limited-competition buy from the original maker, Hydraulic International, Inc., and any vendor holding its letter of authorization. The items are a bulk dispensing unit, a corrosion control cart, a hydraulic fluid purifier, a servicing unit and a tank and pump unit. They support the Navy's MQ-4C and Royal Australian Air Force programs. The notice was posted to satisfy a defense acquisition rule on limited-competition buys.

blocks.title: Coast Guard asks industry about commercial icebreaking vessels for Northeast ports
blocks.text: The U.S. Coast Guard is asking about 'commercially available icebreaking capabilities that may support emergent domestic icebreaking operations within the Coast Guard District Northeast area of responsibility.' This is from a file read today on a notice posted earlier. The request is for information only and is not a solicitation.

footer.coverage_window: November 1-2, 2026 (Pacific time), with a trailing sweep for USAspending contract actions plus the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported, and the apportionment pass flagged no gaps. Of 245 attachments on 56 notices, 206 were not read: 183 are queued for later editions and 23 are access-restricted on SAM.gov. 22 files failed to read this run, and 7,655 files in all are queued. 135 links to outside portals (DIBBS, Navy NECO, PIEE and others) were not followed. Of the five justifications, four had their attached J&A read; the Peraton notice was judged from the notice text alone. Findings Haiku could not verify against the file text were treated as leads and not stated as fact.
